title: RBAC v2 golden fixtures — regression orchestration & CI gating
creator: Asha Chandrasekaran
description:
Scope: Build an end-to-end orchestration layer and CI gating policy for RBAC v2 golden fixtures so that permission regressions are prevented from merging. The goal is a deterministic, fast, and review-actionable regression suite that runs in CI (and on-demand) and produces human-readable diffs and remediation guidance for regressions involving RBAC policy changes, SSO/SAML mappings, and audit log surface area.

What success looks like (Acceptance Criteria):
- A CI job (Buildkite -> GitHub Actions prototype) that runs the RBAC golden regression suite on every PR touching rbac/* or auth/* and fails the PR on any new golden diff.
- Golden fixtures stored in a versioned artifact bucket with immutability metadata and human-friendly manifest (path: s3://redwood-goldens/rbac-v2/).
- Test harness produces an HTML+JSON report linked from the PR showing exact permission matrix diffs, failing scenarios, and suggested mitigations.
- CI run time under 12 minutes for the baseline suite; flaky tests below 2% failure rate.
- Approved fallback flow: if golden failures are detected but flagged as "expected-flaky" by the flaky registry, PR is marked for manual review rather than auto-blocked.

Design notes and trade-offs: 
- Orchestration: prefer Buildkite for isolation and authenticated access to VPC resources (allows running against private Private deployment stack). Prototype GitHub Actions wrapper for community contributors.
- Test environment: Rely on lightweight local emulators for SAML/SSO (urn:mace:shib) rather than full IdP integration to keep tests deterministic. Integrate one end-to-end smoke test against a real SAML IdP in a nightly job to catch integration drift.
- Fixture freshness vs. stability: Keep most fixtures stable; add a separate "update-goldens" flow that requires two approvers and a changelog entry for any golden mutation.
- Resource usage: Use ephemeral K8s jobs with nodeSelector for medium-capacity runners; batch parallel test shards to meet the 12 minute target.

Test matrix highlights:
- Roles x Resources x Actions matrix coverage (admin/read/write/impersonate) for: console, API tokens, runtime endpoints, audit-log export, and dedicated VPC admin actions.
- SAML group-to-role mapping permutations (3 IdP group shapes) + failure modes (missing attribute, expired assertion).
- Audit logging: verify event names, fields present (principal_id, resource, action, outcome), and that sensitive fields are redacted in logs.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Build the harness skeleton (tests/rbac/goldens/orchestrator) and binaries to run fixtures locally with deterministic seeds. 2) Create golden artifact layout and manifest tooling (scripts/goldens/publish). 3) CI integration (Buildkite job + GitHub Actions PR comment reporter). 4) Flaky registry and "expected-flaky" label integration. 5) Nightly end-to-end SAML smoke job. 6) Docs & runbook for updating goldens and handling blocked PRs.

Rollout strategy: start gated on the security/rbac owners team, then enable for all rbac/* and auth/* changes. For the first two weeks, run with a permissive mode (PR comment only) then switch to blocking mode once stability metrics are met.

Paths & artifacts: 
- Golden bucket: s3://redwood-goldens/rbac-v2/
- Prototype PR for harness: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/3892
- CI job config prototype: https://ci.redwood.internal/buildkite/pipelines/rbac-goldens
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/RBAC/RBAC+v2+Golden+Fixtures+Orchestration

Open decisions: 
- Whether to require signed golden updates (git commit signatures + approver list) or rely on repository protections alone. (Security prefers signed updates.)
- Canonical CI runner choice (Buildkite vs GH Actions hybrid).

Risks: 
- Flakiness from SAML emulation if clocks or network latency vary — mitigated by deterministic assertion timestamps and retry logic.
- Storage costs if goldens are over-indexed; mitigate by dedup and gzipped manifests.
